override.title: Your Function Chart gives every function one accountable owner.
override.headline: Your Function Chart gives every function one accountable owner.

notes: At this session it is a check-in. Every leader completed their function scorecard in Metronome as homework.
Ask each leader where their scorecard stands, and which of its two metrics sits on the KFFM.
The scores: 0 below, 1 meets, 2 exceeds. The owner scores first, then their team lead, then they talk about the differences.
Homework: complete the annual reviews on the function scorecards in Metronome.

Purpose in one sentence. Three to five functional accountabilities, each starting Owns. Exactly two metrics: one widget the owner controls and one fiscal metric the role owns. Six to eight key competencies. The company’s core values.
The team agrees its Core Values later today. They then go on every scorecard.

override.title: Test your top three.
override.headline: Test your top three.
override.support: Is it a value you hire and fire on, or a brand value?
notes: A value that fails the tests is a brand value or a wish, not a Core Value.
A fourth or fifth value can earn its place here.
Allow about 10 minutes.
body: When did you last let someone go for not living it?
Does someone who keeps breaching it belong here?
Would you build a new company around it, in any industry?
Then talk about anything important that was left out.

override.title: Is your Market Map still right?
override.headline: Is your Market Map still right?
notes: Put the team’s own Market Map on the screen. The example here is a reminder of its parts.
Ask what changed in the market last quarter. Check that the top competitors are on the map. The team scores them next.
Homework: update the Market Map in the War Room in Metronome.

override.title: Is this still your Core Customer?
override.headline: Is this still your Core Customer?
notes: Put the team’s own Core Customer on the screen. The example here is a reminder of its parts.
Read the three ranked needs aloud. The team tests the white space against them next.
Change only what is no longer true.
Homework: update the Core Customer in the War Room in Metronome.
Ask a leader to read the plan aloud. Invite the team to identify contradictions and untested assumptions.
Test it against the 3HAG line: does each capability build an attribute where the company will lead?
Question the math: do the five widget targets add up to the revenue?
Change only what fails or is no longer true. Anything unresolved goes on the homework list with an owner.
override.support: Read it aloud. Then test it against your 3HAG line.

notes: Read the 1HAG aloud, top to bottom, then run the six checks.
The status review already showed where the 1HAG stands. Test it against the 3HAG line the team drew.
Change only what fails or is no longer true. Anything that fails goes on the homework list with an owner.
override.support: Read it aloud. Then test it against your 3HAG line.

notes: If the answer is no, change the plan now. Move a step, change an owner or drop a priority.
Lanes show the work. They are not the measure of success. That stays on the QHAG.
The weekly leadership meeting reviews sprint lane status.
The team learned these roles at Q1. They now apply to next year’s forecast.
Finance builds the model. Each leader owns the numbers for their widgets. The CEO owns the total.
When the forecast is wrong, the first question is which widget moved, not who to blame.

override.headline: How are your meetings going?
override.title: How are your meetings going?
override.support: For each: running? Working? What to change? Rate it 0, 1 or 2.

panels.heading: Daily huddle
panels.support: 7 to 10 minutes, every day except the day of the weekly meeting. The facilitator rotates.
items: Metrics: yesterday’s widget actual and today’s forecast
The #1 thing to get done today
Stucks, and anything that can’t wait

panels.heading: Weekly 1:1
panels.support: 15 to 30 minutes. Each leader with each direct report, led by the direct report.

panels.heading: Weekly leadership meeting
panels.support: 60 minutes or less. The CEO owns it.
items: Scoreboard: last week’s widget forecast, actual and this week’s forecast
QHAG, priority and sprint lane status

notes: Give it about 10 minutes, on the board’s Meeting Rhythm Check-In.
Rate each meeting: 0 below, 1 meets, 2 exceeds expectations.
All five meetings should be running: the three here, the Monthly Town Hall and Quarterly Planning.
New today: the KFFM review joins the weekly leadership meeting.
